claim_boundary: C021 registers twenty-four attacks. A523 decisively destroys H130's ordinary-Resolution simulation of the full affine dispatcher; the remaining attacks test the repaired non-affine, mixed Res(⊕), and recursive translation descendants.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the full Policy-0T affine shortcut may be polynomial while ordinary Resolution remains exponential
attacks.method: Apply Policy-0T to visible odd-charge Tseitin CNFs on a bounded-degree expander family. The exact local affine recognizer and Gaussian elimination use polynomial work, while classical expander-Tseitin lower bounds require exponential ordinary Resolution size.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the affine branch may still enter recursive search
attacks.method: Run visible odd-charge Tseitin CNFs for K3,3, the cube and Petersen graphs; all return UNSAT with zero recursive calls and one recovered parity equation per vertex.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a finite non-affine trace proof may be misused to support every dispatcher execution
attacks.method: Separate the verified affine_answer=None trace from visible affine executions and check that H130 quantifies over both.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: destroying H130 may also destroy the MAJ3 lower-bound route
attacks.method: Restrict the simulation target to affine_answer=None executions; the C020 MAJ3 audit already places the lifted hard fixture in that branch.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the non-affine trace may still need a hardwired root proof
attacks.method: Construct a translator that consumes the verified trace, lifts local residual resolvents, reverses unit reasons, combines children and emits a newly built root proof.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: deleting assignment-falsified literals may hide weakening
attacks.method: Retain each root-level derived clause, restrict it only for execution, and verify every lifted local resolution line restricts exactly to the recorded residual resolvent.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: terminal conflict clauses may retain implied literals
attacks.method: Resolve conflict clauses backwards through recorded unit reasons in reverse assignment order and verify the returned clause lies inside the entry decision boundary.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the finite translator may hide superlinear overhead or proof depth
attacks.method: Count proof lines and depths on the fixture, then attempt the general recurrence. Constant local overhead is supported finitely, but the universal induction is not yet proved.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the Gaussian shortcut may return only a Boolean answer
attacks.method: Inspect Policy-0T: it counts equations but does not yet emit row-operation provenance or a proof object in Res(⊕).

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: recognized constant-scope affine relations may not have an explicit calculus derivation
attacks.method: Require a verified constant-size translation from every complete local CNF relation to its affine equation; no emitter is present yet.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: ordinary Resolution proofs may not embed into the selected parity calculus
attacks.method: Use the standard inclusion of clause Resolution as a restricted fragment of Res(⊕); exact syntax is deferred to the H133 verifier.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a dispatcher certificate may combine incompatible proof semantics
attacks.method: Demand one verifier that tags affine and clause lines and checks their interface; no complete implementation exists.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: sibling conflicts may require weakening to a common parent clause
attacks.method: Return any derived subclause of the falsified decision boundary. Resolve only when both children retain opposite branch literals; otherwise inherit the child clause already valid at the parent.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the translator may print clauses without legal parent lines
attacks.method: Replay every axiom and Resolution line independently, recompute parent resolvents, final empty clause, width and depth.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: canonical residual merging may lose all root derivations
attacks.method: Keep one legal root proof line per canonical residual and verify that every trace parent remains represented throughout the finite translation.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: depth-one success may fail for direct conflicts, opposite units or multiple propagation batches
attacks.method: Enumerate the missing terminal classes conceptually and design fuzz targets; no complete deeper suite is implemented yet.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: one universal Tear policy may hide incompatible proof strengths in one step
attacks.method: H130 fails precisely because affine and branch reasoning were forced into one weaker proof system; require explicit proof-language dispatch in all future policies.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: the H130 failure may be blamed on memoization
attacks.method: Policy-0T has no cache; its failure comes from affine proof strength, independently confirming that proof-language accounting and cache accounting are distinct resources.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Tseitin local twins may be presented as hard for every proof language
attacks.method: The affine dispatcher decides visible Tseitin before search, preserving the boundary that the family is hard for ordinary Resolution but easy for parity-aware reasoning.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: global parity compression may imply an ordinary clause proof
attacks.method: Separate semantic parity quotienting from ordinary Resolution derivability; H130's failure shows the former need not yield the latter polynomially.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a compact Tear may be treated as proof-system neutral
attacks.method: Require every output quotient or annotation to identify the proof language and certificate cost used to expose its global bit.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: a lower bound for one search core may be generalized to all compilers
attacks.method: Record that H132 begins only after affine dispatch fails and concerns one no-cache DPLL/Resolution core.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: destroying H130 may eliminate the lifted high-treewidth route
attacks.method: The MAJ3 encoding is non-affine to the implemented detector, so H132 retains the exact branch required by the lifting target.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: all polynomial semantic shortcuts may inherit an ordinary proof upper bound
attacks.method: The affine shortcut is not transparent composition of a fixed EF-easy equivalence gadget library; its parity proof strength must be charged separately.
